rules.title: Prohibition on the Sale or Use of Coordinated Pricing Algorithms to Set Rents or Manage Occupancy Levels for Residential Dwelling Units
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley, and it is unlawful for a landlord to use such an algorithm when setting rents or occupancy levels. Each month of violation per unit is a separate violation, enforceable via civil action by the City Attorney or an aggrieved tenant with civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to landlords and vendors with respect to residential dwelling units within the City of Berkeley, prohibiting coordinated pricing algorithms that use nonpublic competitor data to set or recommend rents or occupancy levels.

rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley 
landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy 
levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.

rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making. It is unlawful to inquire about criminal history, indicate persons with criminal backgrounds will not be considered, refuse to rent or terminate tenancy based on criminal history, require disclosure of criminal history, demand higher deposits or rent based on criminal history, refuse to allow addition of family members based on criminal history, or disqualify tenants from rental assistance programs based on criminal history, subject to certain exemptions.
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

rules.title: Written Notice and Opportunity to Respond Required
rules.requirement: If a landlord takes any action against an applicant or tenant based on criminal history, the landlord is required to provide the applicant/tenant with written notice and an opportunity to respond.
rules.quoted_span: If a landlord takes any action against an applicant or tenant based on criminal history (such as refusing to offer a lease, refusing to add a family member, etc.), the landlord is required to provide the applicant/tenant with written notice and an opportunity to respond.

rules.title: Civil Penalties for Fair Chance Ordinance Violations
rules.requirement: Any landlord found to be in violation of the Ordinance shall be subject to administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation, civil damages including actual damages or three times the amount of one month's rent, punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief.
rules.quoted_span: Any landlord found to be in violation of the Ordinance shall be subject to administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation, civil damages including actual damages or three times the amount of one month's rent, punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief.

rules.title: 2026 Relocation Assistance Payment Increase for Owner Move-In and Ellis Act Evictions
rules.requirement: Owners must pay increased relocation assistance to tenants evicted via owner move-in or Ellis Act eviction, with the standard payment increasing to $19,413 and the additional payment for qualifying households increasing to $6,471, effective January 1, 2026.
rules.citation: Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance; Ellis Implementation Ordinance
rules.quoted_span:
The standard relocation assistance payment will increase to
$19,413
.
The additional relocation assistance payment for qualifying households will increase to
$6,471
.

rules.title: Maximum Tenant Screening Fee (2026)
rules.requirement: The maximum tenant screening fee landlords may charge prospective tenants in 2026 is $68.96.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is

rules.title: No Screening Fee If No Unit Available
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot charge a prospective tenant a screening fee if no rental unit is actually available.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord cannot charge a prospective tenant a screening fee if no rental unit is actually available.

rules.title: Reusable Screening Report Must Be Used
rules.requirement: If the tenant provides a reusable screening report, the landlord must use it.
rules.quoted_span: If the tenant provides a reusable screening report, the landlord must use it.

rules.title: Refund of Screening Fee to Non-Selected Applicants
rules.requirement: The landlord must return a screening fee to any applicant not selected, or have a policy under which they review applications in the order received and the first qualified applicant gets the unit, and do not charge a screening fee to any applicant not considered.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord must also return a screening fee to any applicant not selected, or have a policy under which they: (1) review applications in the order received and the first qualified applicant gets the unit, and (2) do not charge a screening fee to any applicant not considered.

rules.title: Notification of Tenant Screening Fee Rights
rules.requirement: When an owner charges a fee to purchase a consumer credit report and to validate, review, or otherwise process an application, the owner must provide a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under state law, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee.
rules.quoted_span: the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under

rules.title: Prohibition of Non-Refundable Fees for Existing Tenancies
rules.requirement: An owner of residential rental property cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.

rules.title: Applicability to Existing Rental Agreements
rules.requirement: Chapter 13.78 applies to all residential rental agreements regardless of any contractual language in any rental agreement or lease to the contrary, and any provision of an existing rental agreement or lease that violates the provisions of this chapter are unenforceable.
rules.quoted_span: Chapter 13.78 applies to all residential rental agreements regardless of any contractual language in any rental agreement or lease to the contrary.

rules.title: Annual General Adjustment Capped at 5%
rules.requirement: The maximum Annual General Adjustment (AGA) that a landlord of a fully-covered rental unit may impose each year is capped at 5%, even if the Rent Ordinance formula would otherwise yield a higher percentage.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, Measure BB Amendments
rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.

rules.title: Minimum Rental Debt Threshold for Nonpayment Eviction
rules.requirement: A landlord may not evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent unless the tenant owes rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent value for a unit of equivalent size.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, Measure BB Amendments
rules.quoted_span: For a landlord to evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent, the tenant must owe an amount of rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent (FMR) value for a unit of equivalent size in the metro area Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR as determined by the US Department of Housing and Urban Development for the fiscal year in which the rent is demanded.

rules.title: No Eviction for Failing to Sign New Fixed-Term Lease
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for failing to sign a substantially similar lease upon expiration of a fixed-term lease.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, Measure BB Amendments
rules.quoted_span: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for failing to sign a substantially similar lease upon expiration of a fixed-term lease.

rules.title: Heightened Standards for Lease Violation Evictions
rules.requirement: To evict a tenant for violation of a material lease term, the term must be mutually agreed upon, the violation must cause substantial, actual damage to the landlord, and the landlord must demonstrate the tenant's behavior was unreasonable.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, Measure BB Amendments
rules.quoted_span:
Material lease terms only include mutually agreed upon lease terms.
The alleged violation must cause substantial, actual damage to the landlord.
The landlord must demonstrate that the tenant’s behavior was unreasonable.

rules.title: Eviction Notice Filing Deadline
rules.requirement: The landlord must file with the Rent Board a copy of any notice to terminate a tenancy, notice to quit, and summons and complaint no later than three business days after the tenant was served with the document.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, Measure BB Amendments
rules.quoted_span: The landlord must file with the Rent Board a copy of any notice to terminate a tenancy, notice to quit, and summons and complaint no later than three business days after the tenant was served with the document.

rules.title: Security Deposit Amount Limit
rules.requirement: Landlords may only charge one month's rent as a security deposit for unfurnished and furnished units, starting July 1, 2024.
rules.quoted_span: Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may only charge one month's rent for unfurnished and furnished units

rules.title: Small Landlord Security Deposit Exception
rules.requirement: Landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total can charge up to two months' rent if ownership is held by a natural person, family trust, or LLC where all members are natural persons.
rules.quoted_span: Starting July 1, 2024, landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total can charge up to two months' rent for furnished and unfurnished units if ownership is held by a natural person, family trust, or limited liability company (LLC) where all members are natural persons

rules.title: Move-Out Walk-Through Inspection Requirement
rules.requirement: Landlords must offer a walk-through inspection during the last two weeks of a tenancy to identify any items that need repair or cleaning.
rules.quoted_span: landlords must offer a walk-through inspection during the last two weeks of a tenancy to identify any items that need repair/cleaning

rules.title: Return of Security Deposit Timeline
rules.requirement: All or any remaining portion of a security deposit must be returned within 21 days after the tenant leaves the unit vacant, with an itemized statement of deductions if applicable.
rules.quoted_span:
All or any remaining portion of a security deposit must be returned
within 21 days
after the tenant/s leave the unit vacant.

rules.title: Proof of Repairs Requirement
rules.requirement: Starting January 1, 2025, landlords must provide proof that necessary repairs were completed when making deductions from a security deposit.
rules.quoted_span: Starting January 1, 2025, landlords must provide proof that necessary repairs were completed.

rules.title: Pre-Tenancy Photograph Requirement
rules.requirement: For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, a landlord must photograph the unit immediately before or at the start of a new tenancy to document the condition of the unit.
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, a landlord must photograph the unit immediately before or at the start of a new tenancy to document the condition of the unit.

rules.title: Post-Move-Out Photograph Requirement
rules.requirement: Starting April 1, 2025, landlords must take photographs of a unit after regaining possession, but before any repairs or cleaning for which the landlord intends to make a deduction from the security deposit.
rules.quoted_span: Starting April 1, 2025, landlords must take photographs of a unit after regaining possession, but before any repairs or cleaning for which the landlord intends to make a deduction from the security deposit.

rules.title: Security Deposit Interest Requirement
rules.requirement: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.
rules.quoted_span: landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year

rules.title: 2026 Annual General Adjustment (AGA)
rules.requirement: Eligible landlords may increase 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than January 1, 2026, with the increase equal to 65% of CPI change for the Bay Area from July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2025.

coverage_conditions.summary: Does not apply to tenancies that began on or after January 1, 2025, and whose rents were set pursuant to the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act.

rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code section 13.76.110A; Rent Board Regulation 1148
rules.quoted_span:
adopted the Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Order for Year 2026 which will allow 
eligible landlords to increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than 
January 1, 2026

rules.title: Rent Control Coverage for Fully Covered Multifamily Units
rules.requirement: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980 are fully covered by Berkeley's rent control, requiring registration and granting just cause eviction and security deposit interest protections.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to most units in multifamily properties built before 1980

rules.requirement: Housing providers receiving DND funding/land or with BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy units may not impose a blanket policy denying housing to anyone with arrests or convictions; applicants must be considered case-by-case.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to housing providers receiving DND funding/land or with income-restricted units under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy.

rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy, p.1
rules.quoted_span:
will not impose a blanket policy that denies 
housing to anyone with arrests and or convictions. Housing providers will consider applicants on 
a case-by-case basis.

rules.requirement: Agents may not consider arrests without conviction, convictions subject to judicial relief, juvenile records, or convictions more than 5 years old when determining housing eligibility or eviction, except where there is a direct relationship to safety risk.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy, p.1

Arrests that did not result in conviction. This includes dismissed charges, diversion

rules.title: Prohibition on Using Credit Score for Housing Decisions
rules.requirement: Agents agree not to use an applicant's credit score to approve or deny housing applications.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy, p.3
rules.quoted_span:
The agent agrees not to use the applicant credit score to approve or deny housing    
applications.

rules.title: Limited Use of Credit History
rules.requirement: Property managers may only use credit history in lieu of rental history to determine ability to pay rent when rental history is not available.

Property Managers may consider an applicant’s credit history, but such information may 
ONLY be used in lieu of rental history to determine an applicant’s ability to pay rent when rental 
history is not available.

rules.title: Lack of Credit History Not Disqualifying

The lack of credit 
history, as opposed to poor credit history, is not sufficient justification to reject an applicant.

rules.requirement: Special legislation petition that would authorize the City of Boston to implement rent stabilization measures, pending further legislative action.

rules.requirement: Special legislation petition that would authorize the City of Boston to implement tenant eviction protections, pending further legislative action.

rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act - Notice of Tenants' Rights
rules.requirement: All landlords planning to end a tenancy agreement must provide the tenant with a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources at the same time as the Notice to Quit or Notice of non-renewal of lease, and must notify the City via an online form with tenant contact information and a copy of the notice.
rules.quoted_span:
The Housing Stability Notification Act requires
ALL LANDLORDS
planning to end a tenancy agreement to provide the tenant with a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources.

rules.title: Failure to Submit Notice to Quit Verification Form
rules.requirement: Landlords who fail to submit the Notice to Quit/Non-renewal of Lease Submission Verification Form through the online portal may be fined up to $300 per day.
rules.quoted_span: Failure to submit this information may result in a fine up to $300 per day.

rules.title: Enforcement and Penalties for HSNA Violations
rules.requirement: Violations of the Housing Stability Notification Act are enforced by Inspectional Services, with a warning for the first offense and a $300 per day fine for the second and subsequent offenses.
rules.quoted_span:

Warning

rules.title: Violation Does Not Halt Eviction

DOES NOT
halt the eviction process.

rules.title: HSNA Enforcement Penalties
rules.requirement: Violations of the HSNA are enforced by the Inspectional Services Department, with a warning for a first offense and a $300 per day fine for subsequent offenses.
rules.quoted_span:
1st Offense: Warning

rules.title: Limits on Use of Criminal History in Tenant Screening
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not consider certain categories of criminal history (arrests without conviction, sealed/expunged records, juvenile records) when screening applicants, and may not impose blanket bans on applicants with any criminal history.
rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.quoted_span: Housing  providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system. Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.

rules.title: Prohibition on Discriminatory Security Deposit Practices Based on Familial Status
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not impose conditions that discriminate against households with children, including charging higher security deposits to families with children.
rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.quoted_span: charging a higher security deposit to households with children or excluding children from playing in common areas open to other tenants

rules.title: Prohibition on Discriminatory Security Deposit Practices Based on Source of Income
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not charge higher security deposits or apply different terms based on an applicant's or tenant's source of income, such as Section 8 vouchers.
rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.quoted_span: charging a higher security deposit for Section 8 applicants or refusing to allow tenants who are using rental assistance from using a pool or other amenities

rules.title: Prohibition on Pet Deposits for Service and Emotional Support Animals
rules.requirement: Tenants with service animals or emotional-support animals cannot be charged pet deposits or pet rent for those animals.
rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.quoted_span: tenants cannot be charged pet deposits or pet rent for them

rules.title: Prohibition on Common Pricing Algorithm Use Under Cartwright Act
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce, or to coerce another person to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term recommended by a common pricing algorithm for the same or similar products or services in California.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.

rules.title: Just Cause Required for Termination of Residential Tenancy
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which must be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy. Just cause includes at-fault reasons (e.g., nonpayment of rent, lease violations, nuisance, waste, criminal activity) and no-fault reasons (e.g., owner move-in, withdrawal from rental market, government order to vacate, demolition or substantial remodel), with relocation assistance or rent waiver required for no-fault terminations.

coverage_conditions.summary: Does not apply to certain exempt properties including transient hotel occupancy, nonprofit hospitals/religious facilities, dormitories, shared living with owner, single-family owner-occupied residences, duplexes with owner occupancy, newer construction (within 15 years), certain small-owner properties with notice, and deed-restricted affordable housing.

rules.quoted_span: after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.

rules.title: Statewide Residential Rent Increase Cap
rules.requirement: An owner of residential real property shall not increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or unit more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10%, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period, based on the lowest gross rental rate charged during the prior 12 months, with no more than two increments over that period.
rules.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.

rules.title: Limit on Number of Rent Increases Per Year
rules.requirement: If the same tenant remains in occupancy over any 12-month period, the gross rental rate shall not be increased in more than two increments over that 12-month period.
rules.quoted_span: the gross rental rate for the unit of residential real property shall not be increased in more than two increments over that 12-month period, subject to the other restrictions of this subdivision governing gross rental rate increase.

rules.title: New Tenancy Rent Setting Exception
rules.requirement: For a new tenancy in which no tenant from the prior tenancy remains in lawful possession, the owner may establish the initial rental rate without the cap applying; the cap applies only to subsequent increases after that initial rate is set.
rules.quoted_span: For a new tenancy in which no tenant from the prior tenancy remains in lawful possession of the residential real property, the owner may establish the initial rental rate not subject to subdivision (a).

rules.title: Exemptions from Statewide Rent Cap
rules.requirement: The rent cap does not apply to deed-restricted affordable housing, dormitories, housing subject to stricter local rent control, housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome), certain single-family/condo properties meeting ownership and notice conditions, and owner-occupied duplexes.
rules.quoted_span: This section shall not apply to the following residential real properties:

rules.title: Notice Requirement for Rent Increases
rules.requirement: An owner shall provide notice of any rent increase under subdivision (a) to each tenant in accordance with Section 827.
rules.quoted_span: An owner shall provide notice of any increase in the rental rate, pursuant to subdivision (a), to each tenant in accordance with Section 827.

rules.title: Sunset Date of Statewide Rent Cap
rules.requirement: This section shall remain in effect until January 1, 2030, and as of that date is repealed.
rules.quoted_span: This section shall remain in effect until January 1, 2030, and as of that date is repealed.

rules.title: Security Deposit Cap - One Month's Rent
rules.requirement: A landlord shall not demand or receive security in an amount exceeding one month's rent, in addition to the first month's rent, except as otherwise provided.
rules.quoted_span: a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy

rules.title: Advance Rent Payment Exception
rules.requirement: The one month's rent security deposit cap does not prohibit an advance payment of not less than six months' rent if the lease term is six months or longer.
rules.quoted_span: This subdivision does not prohibit an advance payment of not less than six months’ rent if the term of the lease is six months or longer

rules.title: Service Member Higher Security Disclosure
rules.requirement: On or after April 1, 2025, if a landlord charges a service member a higher than standard security deposit due to credit history or other factors, the landlord must provide written notice and explanation, and return the additional amount after six months if tenant is not in arrears.
rules.quoted_span: On or after April 1, 2025, if a landlord or its agent charges a service member who rents residential property in which the service member will reside a higher than standard or advertised security pursuant to paragraph (1) due to the credit history, credit score, housing history, or other factor related to the tenant, the landlord shall provide the tenant with a written statement, on or before the date the lease is signed, of the amount of the higher security and an explanation why the higher security amount is being charged

rules.title: Small Landlord Two Months' Rent Exception
rules.requirement: A landlord who is a natural person or LLC of natural persons owning no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four units total may charge up to two months' rent as security deposit, unless the tenant is a service member.
rules.quoted_span: a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to two months’ rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy if the landlord meets both of the following requirements

rules.title: Security Deposit Held in Trust for Tenant
rules.requirement: Any security deposit shall be held by the landlord for the tenant, and the tenant's claim to the security has priority over any creditor of the landlord.
rules.quoted_span: Any security shall be held by the landlord for the tenant who is party to the lease or agreement. The claim of a tenant to the security shall be prior to the claim of any creditor of the landlord

rules.title: No Deduction for Ordinary Wear and Tear
rules.requirement: The landlord shall not assert a claim against the tenant or the security for damages to the premises or defective conditions that preexisted the tenancy, or for ordinary wear and tear.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord shall not assert a claim against the tenant or the security for damages to the premises or any defective conditions that preexisted the tenancy, for ordinary wear and tear or the effects thereof, whether the wear and tear preexisted the tenancy or occurred during the tenancy, or for the cumulative effects of ordinary wear and tear occurring during any one or more tenancies

rules.title: Tenant Right to Initial Move-Out Inspection
rules.requirement: The landlord must notify the tenant in writing of the right to request an initial inspection before move-out and must conduct the inspection upon tenant request, giving at least 48 hours' notice, to allow the tenant to remedy deficiencies before final deductions.
rules.quoted_span: the landlord shall notify the tenant in writing of the tenant’s option to request an initial inspection and of the tenant’s right to be present at the inspection

rules.title: Photographs Required at Move-In
rules.requirement: For tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit immediately before, or at the inception of, the tenancy.
rules.quoted_span:
For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit immediately before, or at the
inception of, the tenancy

rules.title: Photographs Required at Move-Out
rules.requirement: Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit after possession is returned and before repairs or cleanings for which a deduction will be made, and also after such repairs or cleanings are completed.
rules.quoted_span: Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after the possession of the unit is returned to the landlord, but prior to any repairs or cleanings for which the landlord will make a deduction from or claim against the security deposit pursuant to this section, and shall also take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after such repairs or cleanings are completed

rules.title: 21-Day Deadline to Return Deposit and Itemized Statement
rules.requirement: No later than 21 calendar days after the tenant has vacated, the landlord shall furnish the tenant an itemized statement of deductions and return any remaining portion of the security deposit.
rules.quoted_span:
No later than 21 calendar days after the tenant has vacated the premises, but not earlier than the time that either the landlord or the tenant provides a notice to terminate the tenancy under Section 1946 or 1946.1, Section 1161 of the Code of Civil Procedure, or not earlier than 60 calendar days prior to

rules.title: General prohibition on rent control; limited municipal exception
rules.requirement: Cities and towns may not enact, maintain, or enforce rent control of any kind, except that a city or town may accept this chapter and adopt rent control regulation that meets specific conditions, including voluntary compliance after six months, exclusions for small property owners and higher-rent units, and a requirement that the municipality compensate owners from general funds for the difference between fair market rent and controlled rent.
rules.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides:

rules.title: Voluntary compliance after six months
rules.requirement: After six months from the initial adoption of rent control regulation by a city or town, compliance by property owners is entirely voluntary, and property of an owner declining to participate is unaffected by the regulation.
rules.quoted_span: after six months from the date of the initial adoption of rent control regulation by a particular city or town, compliance on the part of property owners as to the rent control regulation or any subsequently adopted rent control regulation shall be entirely voluntary and uncoerced, and the property of a person or entity declining to have his or its property subjected to such regulation shall be wholly unaffected by any aspect of the rent control regulation or any subsequently adopted rent control regulation

rules.title: Scope limitations on local rent control regulation
rules.requirement: Local rent control regulation may not regulate occupancy, services, evictions, condominium conversion, or removal of properties from regulation, and may not apply to rental units owned by an owner with fewer than ten rental units or units with a fair market rent exceeding $400.
rules.quoted_span: such regulation may not include the regulation of occupancy, services, evictions, condominium conversion or the removal of properties from such regulation, nor may such regulation apply to any rental unit that is owned by a person or entity owning less than ten rental units or that has a fair market rent exceeding $400

rules.title: Municipal compensation to owners for rent controlled units
rules.requirement: A municipality adopting rent control regulation must compensate owners of rent controlled units for the difference between the unit's fair market rent and its rent controlled rent, with such compensation paid from the municipality's general funds so that the cost is borne by all taxpayers rather than only the owners of regulated units.
rules.quoted_span: a municipality adopting such regulation shall compensate owners of rent controlled units for each unit in the amount of the difference between the unit's fair market rent and the unit's below market, rent controlled rent, with such compensation coming from the municipality's general funds, so that the cost of any rent control shall be borne by all taxpayers of a municipality and not by the owners of regulated units only

rules.title: Prohibition on Discrimination Against Public Assistance and Housing Subsidy Recipients
rules.requirement: Landlords and persons furnishing rental accommodations or credit may not discriminate against a prospective or current tenant because that person receives federal, state, or local public assistance (including medical assistance) or receives federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements, nor may they discriminate because of any requirement of such assistance or subsidy program.
rules.quoted_span: For any person furnishing credit, services or rental accommodations to discriminate against any individual who is a recipient of federal, state, or local public assistance, including medical assistance, or who is a tenant receiving federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements, because the individual is such a recipient, or because of any requirement of such public assistance, rental assistance, or housing subsidy program.

rules.title: Determination of lease for nonpayment of rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may terminate a tenancy for nonpayment of rent by giving fourteen days' written notice to quit, unless the tenant pays or tenders all rent due, with interest and costs, before the answer is due in a possession action.
rules.quoted_span: Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease, unless the tenant, on or before the day the answer is due, in an action by the landlord to recover possession of the premises, pays or tenders to the landlord or to his attorney all rent then due, with interest and costs of suit.

rules.title: Government payment delay protection against termination for nonpayment
rules.requirement: If nonpayment of rent was caused by delay in a government subsistence or rental payment, the court must continue the hearing at least seven days to notify the agency, and must treat the tenancy as not terminated if all rent, interest, and costs are tendered within that time.
rules.quoted_span: the court in any such action shall continue the hearing not less than seven days in order to furnish notice of such action to the appropriate agency and shall, if all rent due with interest and costs of suit has been tendered to the landlord within such time, treat the tenancy as not having been terminated.

rules.title: Notice to Determine Estate at Will
rules.requirement: Tenancies at will may be terminated by either party with three months' written notice, or if rent is paid at intervals of less than three months, notice equal to the payment interval or thirty days, whichever is longer. For nonpayment of rent, fourteen days' written notice to quit is sufficient, unless the tenant has not received similar notice in the preceding twelve months, in which case the tenant may cure by paying all rent due within ten days of receipt of the notice. Notices for nonpayment must include a statutory notification of the tenant's right to cure.
rules.quoted_span: Estates at will may be determined by either party by three months' notice in writing for that purpose given to the other party; and, if the rent reserved is payable at periods of less than three months, the time of such notice shall be sufficient if it is equal to the interval between the days of payment or thirty days, whichever is longer.

rules.title: Fourteen-Day Notice to Quit for Nonpayment of Rent
rules.requirement: In case of neglect or refusal to pay rent due, fourteen days' written notice to quit is sufficient to terminate a tenancy at will, unless the tenant has not received a similar notice within the preceding twelve months and pays or tenders the full amount of rent due within ten days after receipt of the notice.
rules.quoted_span: In case of neglect or refusal to pay the rent due from a tenant at will, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the tenancy; provided, that the tenancy of a tenant who has not received a similar notice from the landlord within the twelve months next preceding the receipt of such notice shall not be determined if the tenant, within ten days after the receipt thereof, pays or tenders to the landlord, the landlord's attorney, or the person to whom the tenant customarily pays rent, the full amount of any rent due.

rules.title: Required Notification Language in Nonpayment Notices
rules.requirement: Every notice to determine an estate at will for nonpayment of rent must contain a specific notification informing the tenant of their right to prevent termination by paying the full amount of rent due within ten days of receipt, if they have not received such a notice within the preceding twelve months.
rules.quoted_span: Every notice to determine an estate at will for nonpayment of rent shall contain the following notification to the tenant: ''If you have not received a notice to quit for nonpayment of rent within the last twelve months, you have a right to prevent termination of your tenancy by paying or tendering to your landlord, your landlord's attorney or the person to whom you customarily pay your rent the full amount of rent due within ten days after your receipt of this notice.''

rules.title: Extension of Cure Period for Noncompliant Notices
rules.requirement: If a notice to determine an estate at will for nonpayment of rent fails to contain the required statutory notification, the tenant's time to pay or tender rent is extended to the day the answer is due in any action by the landlord to recover possession of the premises.
rules.quoted_span: If any notice to determine an estate at will for nonpayment of rent shall fail to contain such notification, the time within which the tenant receiving the notice would be entitled to pay or tender rent pursuant to this section shall be extended to the day the answer is due in any action by the landlord to recover possession of the premises.

rules.title: Continuance for Delayed Government Payments
rules.requirement: If neglect or refusal to pay rent was caused by a delay in mailing or delivery of a subsistence or rental payment by a government entity, the court must continue the hearing for at least seven days to notify the appropriate agency, and shall treat the tenancy as not terminated if all rent due, with interest and costs, is tendered to the landlord within that time.
rules.quoted_span: If the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due was caused by a failure or delay of the federal government, the commonwealth or any municipality, or any departments, agencies or authorities thereof, in the mailing or delivery of any subsistence or rental payment, check or voucher other than a salary payment to either the tenant or the landlord, the court in any action for possession shall continue the hearing not less than seven days in order to furnish notice of such action to the appropriate agency and shall, if all rent due with interest and costs of suit has been tendered to the landlord within such time, treat the tenancy as not having been terminated.

rules.requirement: A lessor accepting a security deposit must furnish the tenant a written statement of the present condition of the premises, including a comprehensive listing of any existing damage, within specified timeframes.
rules.quoted_span: shall, upon receipt of such security deposit, or within ten days after commencement of the tenancy, whichever is later, furnish to such tenant or prospective tenant a separate written statement of the present condition of the premises to be leased or rented

rules.title: Forfeiture of Security Deposit for Lessor Non-Compliance
rules.requirement: A lessor forfeits the right to retain any portion of a security deposit if they fail to deposit funds properly, fail to provide itemized damage list, use conflicting lease provisions, fail to transfer deposit to successor, or fail to timely return the deposit.
rules.quoted_span: The lessor shall forfeit his right to retain any portion of the security deposit for any reason, or, in any action by a tenant to recover a security deposit, to counterclaim for any damage to the premises if he:

rules.title: Treble Damages for Non-Compliance
rules.requirement: If a lessor fails to comply with certain security deposit requirements, the tenant shall be awarded treble damages plus interest, court costs, and attorney's fees.
rules.quoted_span: the tenant shall be awarded damages in an amount equal to three times the amount of such security deposit or balance thereof to which the tenant is entitled plus interest at the rate of five per cent from the date when such payment became due, together with court costs and reasonable attorney's fees

rules.title: Fee in Lieu of Security Deposit Option
rules.requirement: Beginning August 1, 2025, the executive office of housing and livable communities may authorize lessors and tenants to agree to a fee in lieu of a security deposit, subject to numerous consumer protections including non-discrimination, optionality, and caps on total amount.
rules.citation: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(1)(b)(iii), as amended by 2025, 9, Secs. 54-55
rules.quoted_span: the executive office of housing and livable communities may promulgate regulations to authorize a lessor and a tenant or prospective tenant to agree to the payment of a fee in lieu of payment of a security deposit

rules.title: Security Deposit Remains Tenant's Property
rules.requirement: A security deposit continues to be the property of the tenant, cannot be commingled with lessor's assets, and is not subject to claims of the lessor's creditors.
rules.quoted_span: A security deposit shall continue to be the property of the tenant making such deposit, shall not be commingled with the assets of the lessor, and shall not be subject to the claims of any creditor of the lessor or of the lessor's successor in interest

rules.title: Limitation on Permissible Deductions
rules.requirement: No deduction may be made from the security deposit for any purpose other than those explicitly set forth in the statute, such as unpaid rent, unpaid tax escalation amounts, or damage caused by the tenant.
rules.quoted_span: No deduction may be made from the security deposit for any purpose other than those set forth in this section.

rules.title: Void Lease Provisions Conflicting with Deposit Law
rules.requirement: Any lease provision conflicting with the security deposit statute, or any tenant waiver of its provisions, is void and unenforceable as against public policy.
rules.quoted_span: Any provision of a lease which conflicts with any provision of this section and any waiver by a tenant or prospective tenant of any provision of this section shall be deemed to be against public policy and therefore void and unenforceable.

rules.title: Protection Against Retaliatory Eviction and Reprisals
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from taking reprisals against tenants for reporting code violations, joining tenant unions, or exercising legal rights; receipt of a termination notice, rent increase, or substantial alteration of tenancy terms within six months of protected tenant activity creates a rebuttable presumption of retaliation, rebuttable only by clear and convincing evidence of independent justification; any lease waiver of this protection is void.
rules.quoted_span: The receipt of any notice of termination of tenancy, except for nonpayment of rent, or, of increase in rent, or, of any substantial alteration in the terms of tenancy within six months after the tenant has commenced, proceeded with, or obtained relief in such action, exercised such rights, made such report or complaint, or organized or joined such tenants' union or within six months after any other person has taken such action or actions on behalf of the tenant or in, or relating to, the building in which the tenant resides, shall create a rebuttable presumption that such notice or other action is a reprisal against the tenant for engaging in such activities.

rules.title: Broker/Finder Fee Payment Restriction for Rental Housing
rules.requirement: A licensed broker or salesperson may only contract with a prospective tenant to find rental residential property or with a landlord to find a tenant, and any fee for such services may only be paid by the party who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the broker or salesperson, preventing landlords from shifting broker fees onto tenants who did not hire the broker.
rules.citation: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 112, § 87DDD 1/2 (as amended by 2025, 9, Sec. 43, effective August 1, 2025)
rules.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson.

rules.title: Licensing Requirement for Finding Dwelling Accommodations for a Fee
rules.requirement: No person may engage in the business of finding dwelling accommodations for prospective tenants for a fee unless that person is a licensed broker or salesman as defined under section 87PP of chapter 112.
rules.citation: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 112, § 87DDD 1/2 (text effective until August 1, 2025)
rules.quoted_span: No person shall engage in the business of finding dwelling accommodations for prospective tenants for a fee unless such person is a licensed broker or salesman as defined in section eighty-seven PP of chapter one hundred and twelve.

rules.title: Notice to Quit for Nonpayment of Rent Requirements
rules.requirement: A landlord's written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent must be accompanied by a form containing documentation of repayment agreements, information on rental assistance programs, applicable court rules/orders on summary process, and relevant legal restrictions on evictions, along with a prominent statement informing the tenant that the notice is not an eviction and that only a court order can force them to leave. Courts may not accept eviction filings for nonpayment of rent without proof of delivery of this form.
rules.quoted_span: A notice to quit for nonpayment of rent given in writing by a landlord to a residential tenant pursuant to this chapter shall be accompanied by a form that shall include, but not be limited to: (i) documentation of any agreements between the tenant and landlord for the tenant to repay the landlord for nonpayment of rent

rules.title: Mandatory Eviction Notice Statement
rules.requirement: The notice form must prominently display a statement informing tenants that a notice to quit is not an eviction, that they do not need to immediately leave, that they are entitled to a legal proceeding to defend against the eviction, and that only a court order can force them to leave.
rules.quoted_span: THIS NOTICE TO QUIT IS NOT AN EVICTION. YOU DO NOT NEED TO IMMEDIATELY LEAVE YOUR UNIT. YOU ARE ENTITLED TO A LEGAL PROCEEDING IN WHICH YOU CAN DEFEND AGAINST THE EVICTION. ONLY A COURT ORDER CAN FORCE YOU TO LEAVE YOUR UNIT.

rules.title: Court Filing Requirement for Nonpayment Eviction
rules.requirement: No court with jurisdiction over summary process actions, including the Boston municipal court department, may accept for filing a writ, summons, or complaint in an eviction for nonpayment of rent for a residential dwelling unit without proof of delivery of the required notice-to-quit form.
rules.quoted_span: No court having jurisdiction over an action for summary process pursuant to chapter 239, including the Boston municipal court department, shall, in an eviction for nonpayment of rent for a residential dwelling unit, accept for filing a writ, summons or complaint without proof of delivery of the form required under this section.

rules.title: Prohibition on Criminal Record Inquiries Prior to Conditional Offer
rules.requirement: A housing provider shall not require an applicant to complete any housing application that includes any inquiries regarding an applicant's criminal record prior to the provision of a conditional offer, nor make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant's criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.
rules.quoted_span:
A
housing provider
shall not require an applicant to
complete any housing application that includes any inquiries regarding an
applicant’s criminal record prior to the provision of a conditional offer

rules.title: Prohibited Criminal Record Considerations
rules.requirement: A housing provider shall not, either before or after the issuance of a conditional offer, evaluate an applicant based on arrests or charges that have not resulted in a criminal conviction, expunged convictions, convictions erased through executive pardon, vacated and otherwise legally nullified convictions, juvenile adjudications of delinquency, and records that have been sealed.

rules.title: Limited Lookback Periods for Criminal Record Consideration After Conditional Offer
rules.requirement: After a conditional offer, a housing provider may only consider certain serious convictions, or indictable offenses within specified lookback periods: six years for first-degree offenses, four years for second- or third-degree offenses, and one year for fourth-degree offenses.
rules.quoted_span:
is for an indictable offense of the first degree
that was issued, or if the conviction resulted in a prison sentence that
sentence concluded, within the six years immediately preceding the issuance of
the conditional offer

rules.title: Disclosure Requirement Before Accepting Application Fee
rules.requirement: Prior to accepting any application fee, a housing provider shall disclose in writing to the applicant whether the eligibility criteria include review of criminal history and a statement regarding the applicant's right to provide evidence of inaccuracies or rehabilitation.
rules.quoted_span:
Prior to
accepting any application fee, a housing provider shall disclose in writing to
the applicant:
(1)   Whether the eligibility criteria of the housing
provider include the review and consideration of criminal history

rules.title: Prohibition on Drug or Alcohol Testing Requirement
rules.requirement: A housing provider shall not require an applicant to submit to a drug or alcohol test, or request the applicant's consent to obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.
rules.quoted_span:
A housing provider shall not require an applicant
to submit to a drug or alcohol test, or request the applicant’s consent to
obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.

rules.title: Prohibition on Discriminatory Housing Advertisements Based on Criminal Record
rules.requirement: A housing provider shall not knowingly or purposefully publish, or cause to be published, any housing advertisement that explicitly provides that the housing provider will not consider any applicant who has been arrested or convicted of one or more crimes or offenses, with limited exceptions.
rules.quoted_span:
A housing provider shall not knowingly or
purposefully publish, or cause to be published, any housing advertisement that
explicitly provides that the housing provider will not consider any applicant
who has been arrested or convicted of one or more crimes or offenses

rules.title: Residential Rental Property Application Fee Cap
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not charge an application or similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property exceeding $50, subject to annual CPI adjustment, with exemptions for one/two-family dwellings and certain real estate licensees.

coverage_conditions.summary: Does not apply to one-family or two-family dwellings offered for rent, or to licensees of the New Jersey Real Estate Commission unless the licensee is the landlord.

rules.quoted_span:
A landlord, or
agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply
to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which
exceeds $50.

rules.title: Penalties for Violating Application Fee Cap
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent who charges an application fee exceeding $50 is liable for a penalty of up to $500 for a first offense, up to $750 for a second offense, and up to $1,000 for each subsequent offense, enforced under the Penalty Enforcement Law of 1999, with wrongfully charged amounts remitted to the applicant.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord, or agent thereof, who violates
subsection a. of this section shall be liable for a penalty of up to $500 for a
first offense, up to $750 for a second offense, and up to $1,000 for each
subsequent offense

rules.title: No Statewide Rent Control; Municipal Rent Control Authorized
rules.requirement: New Jersey has no state law establishing, governing, or controlling rents; municipalities may pass ordinances establishing rent control or rent leveling, enforced by locally created boards.
rules.quoted_span:
The State of New Jersey has no laws that establish, govern or control rents. Municipalities 
may pass an ordinance establishing rent control or rent leveling.

rules.title: Newly Constructed Dwellings Exempt from Local Rent Control
rules.requirement: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years following completion of construction of the building.
rules.quoted_span:
newly 
constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period 
of 30 years following completion of construction of the building

rules.title: Rent Increases Must Not Be Unconscionable
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot raise rent mid-lease; the old lease must be terminated and a new lease offered with the increased rent, and the increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with municipal ordinances governing rent increases.
rules.quoted_span:
The increase in rent must not be 
unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest 
person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act Protection from Eviction Without Good Cause
rules.requirement: A landlord may recover possession of a dwelling unit used as a residence only by consent of the tenants or through the legal process of eviction, and must have good cause to evict a tenant.
rules.quoted_span:
The Anti-Eviction Act,  N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1 to 61.12, was created to protect 
blameless tenants from eviction and was adopted in recognition of the housing shortage in 
the State.

rules.title: Maximum Security Deposit Amount
rules.requirement: The maximum security deposit a landlord may collect cannot be more than one and one-half times one month's rent.
rules.quoted_span:
The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than 
one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ).

rules.title: Limit on Annual Security Deposit Increase
rules.requirement: Any additional yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.
rules.quoted_span:
Any additional 
yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.

rules.title: Timely Return of Security Deposit
rules.requirement: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant.
rules.quoted_span:
Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security 
deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1).

rules.title: Interest Payment on Security Deposit
rules.requirement: The interest or earnings paid on the security deposit belongs to the tenant and must be paid to the tenant in cash or credited toward rent due on the renewal or anniversary of the lease, or on January 31 if proper written notice has been given.
rules.quoted_span:
The interest or earnings paid on the security deposit belongs to the tenant and shall be paid 
to the tenant in cash or credited toward rent due and owing on the ren ewal or anniversary of the 
tenant’s lease or on January 31,  if the tenant has been given written notice, that the interest 
payments will be paid on January 31 of each year (N.J.S.A. 46:8-19 (c)).

rules.title: Double Damages for Wrongfully Withheld Deposit
rules.requirement: If a landlord fails to return the security deposit within 30 days or the tenant disagrees with deductions, the tenant may sue for double the amount wrongfully withheld, plus court costs and attorney's fees.
rules.quoted_span:
If a landlord fails to return the security deposit within 30 days, or the tenant disagrees with 
the amount deducted, the tenant may sue for double the amount of the security deposit that the 
tenant contends was wrongfully withheld.

rules.title: Reasonable Rental Application Fees Permitted
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge the tenant for the cost of a credit report and may also request reasonable rental application fees or employment verification.
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord is allowed 
to charge the tenant for the cost of the report. The landlord may also request reasonable rental 
application fees or employment verification.

rules.title: Adverse Action Disclosure for Credit Denials
rules.requirement: If a tenant's application is denied due to their credit report, the landlord must provide the tenant with the name, address, and telephone number of the credit reporting or screening agency that supplied the negative report.
rules.quoted_span:
If a tenant’s  application is denied due their credit report, the landlord must 
provide the tenant with the name, address, and telephone number of the credit reporting or 
screening agency that supplied the negative report (15 U.S.C.A. § 1681m).

rules.title: Source of Income Protection in Housing
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot deny housing to a lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher or other lawful source of income or rent payment.
rules.quoted_span:
The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination  based
on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent
or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses. This
means, for example, that a landlord cannot deny the
lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to
rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful
income.

rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for a rental property owner to use a coordinator's services, for a coordinator to facilitate agreements restricting competition or perform a coordinating function, for persons to engage in parallel pricing coordination, or for any person to perform a coordinating function, with respect to residential dwelling unit pricing.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies statewide to rental property owners and coordinators using algorithmic devices to set rents or coordinate pricing for residential dwelling units.

rules.quoted_span:
a rental property owner, or any agent,
representative, or subcontractor thereof, to receive, subscribe to, contract
for, or otherwise exchange any form of consideration in return for the use of,
the services of a coordinator

rules.title: FAIR Act - Definition of Algorithmic Device and Coordinating Function
rules.requirement: Defines algorithmic devices and coordinating functions used to set or recommend rental prices, material lease terms, or occupancy levels using competitively sensitive information, which are subject to the act's prohibitions.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies statewide to algorithmic devices and software used by landlords to process rental pricing data.

rules.quoted_span:
collecting the competitively sensitive
information of two or more rental property owners for the purpose of analyzing
or processing information through the use of an algorithm or other automated
process, including by using the information to train an algorithm, where the
algorithm or other automated process is used to set or recommend rental prices,
material lease terms, or occupancy levels

rules.title: FAIR Act - Local Preemption Provision
rules.requirement: A municipality is prohibited from enacting an ordinance that conflicts with this act, though it does not prohibit ordinances explicitly authorized or required by other law.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies statewide, limiting municipal ordinances that conflict with the FAIR Act's algorithmic rent-setting prohibitions.

rules.quoted_span:
A municipality shall be prohibited from enacting
an ordinance that conflicts with this act.  This subsection shall not be
construed to prohibit the enactment of ordinances explicitly authorized or
required by any other law.

rules.title: Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy
rules.requirement: A landlord may not terminate a residential tenancy covered by this Division without just cause, which includes specified at-fault and no-fault grounds.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this 
Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.

rules.title: No-Fault Just Cause: Owner Move-In Requirements
rules.requirement: An owner may terminate a tenancy for no-fault just cause to occupy the unit as a primary residence for the owner or specified relatives for at least 12 continuous months, in good faith.
rules.quoted_span:
The owner seeks to recover possession to occupy the residential rental 
property for the owner or their spouse, domestic partner, child (by 
blood or adoption), grandchild (by blood or adoption), parent, or 
grandparent for a minimum of 12 continuous months as that person’s 
primary residence.

rules.title: No-Fault Just Cause: Demolition or Substantial Remodel
rules.requirement: A landlord may terminate a tenancy for no-fault just cause to demolish or substantially remodel the unit, subject to permit posting and notice requirements.
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord seeks to recover possession to demolish or to 
substantially remodel the residential rental property.

rules.title: Notice of At-Fault Termination to Tenant
rules.requirement: Before terminating for a curable at-fault violation, the landlord must first give written notice of the violation with an opportunity to cure.
rules.quoted_span:
Before a landlord issues a notice to terminate a 
tenancy for at-fault just cause that is a curable lease violation, the 
landlord shall first give written notice of the violation including a 
description of the violation and an opportunity to cure the violation

rules.title: Notice of No-Fault Termination to Tenant
rules.requirement: For no-fault terminations, landlords must give written notice at least 30 or 60 days prior to the proposed termination date, including basis for termination and relocation assistance rights.
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord shall give written notice to the tenant 
at least 30 or 60 days prior to the proposed date of termination as 
required by California Civil Code section 1946.1, as may be amended, 
in no less than 12-point font.

rules.title: Relocation Assistance for No-Fault Terminations - Standard Amount
rules.requirement: Landlords must provide relocation assistance equal to two months of actual rent to tenants terminated for no-fault just cause, regardless of income or tenancy length.
rules.quoted_span:
the direct 
payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to 
two months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in 
effect at the date of the notice.

rules.title: Relocation Assistance for Senior or Disabled Tenants
rules.requirement: If the tenant is a senior or disabled, relocation assistance for no-fault termination must equal three months of actual rent instead of two.
rules.quoted_span:
If the tenant is a senior or disabled, the direct payment 
to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to three 
months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in effect 
at the date of the notice.

rules.title: Right to Re-Rent Offer After No-Fault Eviction
rules.requirement: If a unit is offered for rent again within five years of a no-fault eviction under specified grounds, the landlord must first offer to lease the unit back to the displaced tenant who timely requested such an offer.
rules.quoted_span:
landlord shall first offer to lease the 
residential rental property in writing to the tenant displaced from that unit by 
the no-fault just cause termination if the tenant:

rules.title: Void Termination Notice for Non-Compliance
rules.requirement: A landlord's failure to comply with the termination and relocation requirements of this Division renders any termination notice void.
rules.quoted_span:
a landlord’s failure to comply with any provision of this Division shall 
render void any notice of termination required by this Division.

rules.title: Screening Criteria Disclosure for Re-Rent Offers
rules.requirement: When offering to re-rent to a previously displaced tenant, the landlord may screen the tenant using industry accepted methods but must communicate the minimum screening criteria in the written offer.
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord shall have the right to screen the tenant using industry accepted 
methods and shall communicate the minimum screening criteria in the written 
offer for the new tenancy.

rules.title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing Ordinance
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord, and it is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
rules.quoted_span:
(a) It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an
algorithmic device to a landlord.
(b) It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates
or occupancy levels for residential rental property.

rules.title: Definition of Algorithmic Device
rules.requirement: An algorithmic device is defined as software or a product that uses nonpublic competitor data concerning rental rates, occupancy levels, or other leasing information to advise or recommend rental rates or occupancy levels to a landlord, with exceptions for aggregated public data reports and affordable housing program compliance tools.
rules.quoted_span:
Algorithmic device means a software or product that uses or incorporates one or
more algorithms to perform calculations of nonpublic competitor data concerning
rental rates, occupancy levels, or other information regarding the leasing of
residential rental property to advise a landlord on, or recommend to a landlord,
rental rates or occupancy levels that may be achieved for a residential rental
property in the City of San Diego.

rules.title: Remedies for Algorithmic Rent-Setting Violations
rules.requirement: A tenant may seek injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation against a landlord who uses a prohibited algorithmic device, and a prevailing tenant shall recover costs and reasonable attorney's fees.
rules.quoted_span:
A tenant may seek injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to
$1,000 per violation of this Division, in a civil action against a landlord.
In an action brought under this Division, a prevailing tenant shall recover
costs and reasonable attorney’s fees.

rules.title: Fair Chance Ordinance - Affordable Housing Protections
rules.requirement: Protects residents with arrest or conviction history from discrimination in affordable housing decisions.
rules.quoted_span: San Francisco's Fair Chance Ordinance protects residents with arrest or conviction history in affordable housing decisions.

rules.title: Just Cause Required for Eviction
rules.requirement: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction, and the mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute just cause.
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction. Note that the mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute "just cause" for eviction.

rules.title: Just Cause Required to Remove Housing Services
rules.requirement: The landlord also needs a just cause reason to take away or remove access to certain housing services, including but not limited to garage facilities, parking facilities, driveways, storage spaces, and laundry rooms.
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord also needs a "just cause“ reason to take away or remove access to certain
housing services
, including but not limited to garage facilities, parking facilities, driveways, storage spaces, and laundry rooms.

rules.title: Just Cause Eviction Protections Extend to Certain Exempt Tenancies
rules.requirement: Some tenancies that are exempt from the rent increase limitations of the Ordinance, including newly constructed rental units with Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979 and tenancies eligible for increases under Costa-Hawkins, are still subject to just cause eviction requirements.
rules.quoted_span: Some tenancies that are exempt from the rent increase limitations of the Ordinance are still subject to the eviction provisions of the Ordinance, and tenants in these categories can only be evicted for one of the “just cause” reasons listed in the Ordinance.

rules.title: Annual Allowable Rent Increase for Rent-Controlled Units (2026-2027)
rules.requirement: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable rent increase effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is capped at 1.6%.
rules.citation: SF Rent Board Annual Rent Increase Announcement
rules.quoted_span: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.

rules.title: Prohibition on Algorithmic Devices for Setting Rents
rules.requirement: Prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco; allows a tenant or the City Attorney to bring a civil action for violations.
rules.quoted_span: adding Section 37.10C to the Rent Ordinance went into effect on October 14, 2024. The law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.

rules.title: Relocation Payments for Owner/Relative Move-in, Demolition, Capital Improvement, or Substantial Rehabilitation Evictions
rules.requirement: Landlords evicting tenants based on Owner/Relative Move-in, Demolition/Permanent Removal of Unit from Housing Use, Temporary Capital Improvement Work, or Substantial Rehabilitation must pay relocation amounts per tenant, up to a maximum per unit, with additional amounts due for elderly, disabled, or households with minor children, as set by the Rent Board on an annual basis.
rules.quoted_span: Relocation Payments for Evictions based on Owner/Relative Move-in OR Demolition/Permanent Removal of Unit from Housing Use OR Temporary Capital Improvement Work* OR Substantial Rehabilitation

rules.title: Relocation Payments for Ellis Act Evictions
rules.requirement: Landlords evicting tenants under the Ellis Act must pay relocation amounts per tenant, up to a maximum per unit, with additional amounts due for elderly (62 years or older) or disabled tenants, as set by the Rent Board on an annual basis.
rules.citation: California Ellis Act; SF Rent Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Relocation payments for tenants evicted under the Ellis Act

rules.title: Relocation Payments for Short-Term Capital Improvement Evictions
rules.requirement: The amount of relocation payments for temporary capital improvement evictions lasting less than 20 days is governed by state law rather than the local Rent Ordinance provision covering longer displacements.
rules.quoted_span: The amount of relocation payments for temporary capital improvement evictions for less than 20 days is governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9 and not by Rent Ordinance Section 37.9C.

rules.title: Allowable Annual Rent Increase (2026-2027)
rules.requirement: Landlords subject to the San Francisco Rent Ordinance may increase rent by no more than 1.6% during the period March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027.
rules.quoted_span: 1.6% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027

rules.title: Security Deposit Interest Rate (2026-2027)
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay tenants interest on security deposits at a rate of 4.2% for the period March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027.
rules.quoted_span: 4.2% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027

rules.title: Relocation Payments for Owner Move-In, Demolition, or Substantial Rehabilitation Evictions
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay relocation benefits to tenants evicted for owner/relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal of a unit from housing use, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation.
rules.quoted_span: Relocation Payments for Evictions based on Owner/Relative Move-in OR Demolition/Permanent Removal of Unit from Housing Use OR Temporary Capital Improvement Work* OR Substantial Rehabilitation

rules.title: Relocation Payments for Ellis Act Evictions
rules.requirement: Landlords who evict tenants under the Ellis Act must pay relocation payments as set forth in the Rent Ordinance.
rules.quoted_span: Relocation payments for tenants evicted under the Ellis Act

rules.title: Relocation Payments for Temporary Displacement Less Than 20 Days
rules.requirement: For temporary capital improvement evictions resulting in displacement of less than 20 days, relocation payments are governed by state law rather than the Rent Ordinance.
rules.quoted_span: is governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9 and not by Rent Ordinance Section 37.9C.

rules.title: Maximum Allowable Rent Increase
rules.requirement: Rent increases are capped at 3% of current rent or 80% of the CPI change, whichever is less. The current maximum allowable rent increase is 2.87% for September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027.
rules.citation: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The increase cannot be more than 3% of your current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.

rules.title: Just Cause Evictions Required
rules.requirement: Landlords must have a valid reason to evict a tenant, such as not paying rent, breaking the lease, or the landlord wanting to move into the property themselves.
rules.citation: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you. This could be for not paying rent, breaking the lease, or if the landlord wants to move into the property themselves.

rules.title: Rent Stabilization Ordinance - Annual Rent Increase Cap
rules.requirement: Residential rent increases are limited to the lower of 3% per year or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period; if the CPI is negative, no rent increase is permitted.

coverage_conditions.summary: The rent cap does not apply to residential buildings constructed after February 1, 1995, or to mobile home spaces offered for rent after January 1, 1990.

rules.quoted_span: Increase in residential rents are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period. If the CPI is negative, no rent increase is permitted.

rules.title: Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.requirement: After the first 30 days of tenancy, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which must be stated in a written notice, with specified at-fault and no-fault causes allowed.

coverage_conditions.summary: The Just Cause Ordinance shall not apply to certain types of residential property, including housing produced in the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable housing; hotel and transient occupancy; hospital and care facilities; dormitories; and other shared living quarters.
